_comment: Services whose container health signal cannot go red for a real outage, recorded
rather than quietly tolerated. scripts/check_health_claims.py enforces the shape:
an entry with no reason, no owner, or a past expiry is itself a failure, because a
stale waiver is another claim nobody checks.
Both entries below are OPEN DEBT, not settled design. The incident they describe
has already happened: on 2026-07-25 a client tenant sat at /readyz 503 for about
forty minutes on an unapplied schema head while `docker ps` reported the kernel
healthy the whole time. Nothing in the orchestration layer could see it.
They are exemptions and not fixes because pointing the kernel healthcheck at
/readyz is a live-deployment behaviour change with its own blast radius, and it
is not one to make in the same commit as the gate that found it.

kernel.reason: The healthcheck probes /healthz (liveness) while the app also serves /readyz. Moving it is the correct fix and is deliberately deferred: /readyz consults the Alembic head AND the fleet's signed stack-tool receipt AND the Hatchet probe, so a dead fleet-worker or an unconfigured signing key would flip the kernel unhealthy, and channel-gateway plus pi-sidecar carry `depends_on: service_healthy` on it - the change alters what that dependency means. It needs a deployment window and a rehearsal against a real tenant, not a green gate. Until then this waiver states the exposure plainly: this healthcheck cannot detect the outage that has already happened once.

fleet-worker.reason: The probe is `python -c "import boltrig"`, which proves the interpreter can import a module and nothing else - not that the pump is claiming work, not that it can reach the store. It is exempt rather than fixed because `python -m boltrig.api.worker` serves no HTTP at all, so there is no readiness endpoint to point at; inventing a requirement it cannot satisfy would make the gate a lie in the other direction. It is not exempt from the GOAL: it already publishes a signed, short-lived stack-tool receipt to Redis that the kernel's /readyz consumes, so the real fix is a `boltrig fleet health` command that reads that receipt and exits non-zero when it is stale or absent.
